title: Sensex gains 390 points as IT shares rally; Wipro to take on 3,000 bp finance staff
dek: HCL Tech, TCS and Infosys led a volatile session; the rupee slipped 24 paise to 92.44 a dollar on oil prices and US tariff worries. Wipro's new bp deal covers finance staff in India, Hungary and Malaysia.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
India's main stock indices closed higher on Thursday after a choppy session, led by information technology shares. The BSE Sensex rose 390.31 points, or 0.46%, to 84,328.59, after swinging nearly 800 points between a low of 83,754.66 and a high of 84,551.74. The NSE Nifty 50 gained 65.25 points, or 0.25%, to 25,884.50.

The gains extended Wednesday's sharp rebound, when the Sensex jumped 1,502 points. Reports linked Thursday's caution to uncertainty over the India-US trade talks after Washington proposed tariffs of up to 25% on Indian goods, or 17% if a deal is signed. The US Trade Representative's proposal, announced on Wednesday after investigations into what Washington calls "structural excess capacity" in 14 economies, is not yet in force: it opens a comment period to 5 January 2027. India's commerce ministry has rejected the finding and said trade concerns should be settled through bilateral talks.

## Gainers and losers

IT stocks led the market. HCL Technologies rose about 5.6%, Tata Consultancy Services about 3.5% and Infosys about 2.7%, according to market data reported after the close; metal and realty shares also gained. Asian Paints, Bajaj Finance, Shriram Finance and Trent were among the biggest losers, and consumer durables, auto and media indices lagged. Telecom and FMCG shares also saw selling. Smaller companies did slightly better than the benchmarks: in late trade the BSE 150 MidCap index was up about 0.2% and the BSE 250 SmallCap index about 0.6%, according to reports. Among smaller companies, Diamond Power Infrastructure rose more than 2% after it told investors it had received conductor supply orders worth about ₹413.7 crore, excluding GST, from Adani Energy Solutions, reports said.

The rupee weakened 24 paise to close at 92.44 against the US dollar, according to reports, pressured by crude oil prices and the proposed US tariffs, though inflows from foreign investors limited its fall. On the commodity exchange, gold rose about 1.1% to around ₹1,22,510 per 10 grams while silver fell more than 3%, reports said.

## Wipro's bp deal

Wipro shares rose more than 4% during the day after the British energy company bp announced a strategic partnership under which about 3,000 bp employees who support its finance operations in India, Hungary and Malaysia will move to Wipro.

In its announcement, dated 25 November, bp said the deal was meant to transform its core finance operations and improve long-term cost competitiveness using AI, automation and process changes. The new operating model is expected to take effect in 2027, subject to applicable conditions. bp said it would keep overall accountability for standards, controls, data and technology governance, with PwC providing oversight of controls.

"We believe this partnership with Wipro is the best path forward for bp and our people," said Kate Thomson, bp's chief financial officer. Srini Pallia, Wipro's chief executive, said the engagement underscored the company's "deep domain expertise" and welcomed the transferring staff. The companies did not disclose the value of the contract.

## What to watch

Markets will look to India's second-quarter GDP figures, due at the end of November, and any progress in the trade talks with the US.
